With the default revalidate_instances='never', Item.model_validate(copied, strict=True) ordinarily returns that existing instance without checking its fields, so it does not reject the string. deep=True changes copying depth, not validation. Direct Item(quantity='invalid') fails integer validation under strict=True. Assigning original.quantity raises a frozen-instance ValidationError, even when the new value is otherwise valid. To validate ordinary input, pass a mapping such as Item.model_validate({'quantity': 'invalid'}, strict=True), or revalidate the copied object's dumped data with Item.model_validate(copied.model_dump(), strict=True); dumping an invalid field may emit a serialization warning. To validate existing instances, configure revalidate_instances='always' on the model being validated. Then model_validate(copied, strict=True) checks the fields and rejects this value. 'subclass-instances' does not revalidate an exact Item instance.
